While the story is well-written and atmospheric, it is a realistic slice-of-life vignette depicting a mundane morning commute on a cable ferry. It focuses on sensory details, routine, and quiet, understated human interactions (including a brief, unexplained moment of personal avoidance at the very end when Ilse ignores a phone call). Because it simply observes everyday life and common human behaviors without exploring novel concepts, challenging beliefs, or delving into deep thematic territory, an average reader will not obtain a unique or original idea from reading it.
